Run Results

Navigate the Output tab

Area What to inspect
Last Run Execution Results Step status and errors
Messages Text from Show Message
Charts / Live Monitors Charts and current monitor view
Foreground Output Output Pages, statistics and data
Background Output Captured datasets, statistics and data

Last Run is the current result workspace. Execution records and committed rows appear newest first; Messages appear in production order. Enabled Live Monitors appear below Charts.

Last Run: the most recent execution

Note: Orchestrator retains the latest run, not a test-record database. Export measurement data before starting a new run or leaving the application if you need to retain it.

Desktop keeps one Last Run in memory. It does not provide Run History, a database, or SQL storage.

At run start, Desktop saves a Workflow snapshot for that run. Editing the current Workflow afterward does not reinterpret the Last Run. Opening a Template clears the Last Run, and Clear Last Run removes the current in-memory result and snapshot.

Last Run also keeps the Execution Mode captured when that run started. Its Simulation or Live badge does not change when the current selector changes, so a simulated success is never presented as a real-hardware success.

If a run did not fully complete, committed rows remain available as partial results and can be manually exported after execution stops.

Inspect and collapse result panels

Area Selection and export
Foreground Output Source selects an Output Page and updates Summary, Output Data and export scope.
Background Output Source selects Background and Capture Dataset, with Worker status. Pages contain 100 rows; paging appears only when needed.

Both sections put export controls in Export settings below Output Data. Foreground chooses a file or folder according to scope; Background always chooses a destination folder and exports the full selected or all datasets, not just the visible rows. Its export button names the chosen format.

Both share Auto, Fixed and Raw number display settings without changing stored data or export precision. Background statistics show only available dataset values; Scopes retains Valid/Invalid, while Serial RX shows event and byte counts. Foreground pages and background datasets are selected separately.

Charts, optional Live Monitors, Foreground Output and Background Output, each Chart and Live Monitor, and both Output sections' Summary and Output Data have independent − / + controls. All start expanded. Collapsing hides content without clearing settings, removing Charts, stopping Capture or pausing Monitor reception. Collapse state is not saved with Templates.

When Charts is collapsed, Save charts with template and the chart count remain visible.

Last Run Execution Results and Messages each have a + / − control on the right of their heading. Both start expanded, and each collapses on its own without affecting the other. Collapsing changes what is displayed only: it never removes execution data, stops a run, or clears results. Expanding again restores the same position in the result list.

When Last Run Execution Results is collapsed it keeps its heading, the Execution Mode badge, and the execution count summary. The execution list and its Newer / Older paging are hidden until it is expanded.

Read error feedback

Failed runs and failed execution records show a short plain-language explanation first. The original error remains visible under Technical details for debugging. This extra explanation appears only for failures; successful and cancelled execution records keep the existing compact display. Instrument-specific SCPI/VISA details are preserved rather than reinterpreted by Desktop.

Messages

Setting or limit Behavior
Message 1 / 2 / 3 Three independent tabs
Order Oldest at top, newest below
Retention Most recent 1,000 per tab; summary shows the total count
Message length Up to 4,096 characters; longer values are truncated
Export Not available

Messages collects the text written by Show Message steps. It has three independent tabs, Message 1, Message 2, and Message 3, and a step chooses which one it writes to. Each tab lists its messages in the order the workflow produced them, oldest first, so a loop reads top to bottom. This is the opposite of Last Run Execution Results and Output Data, which are shown newest first. A message keeps its own line breaks. Switching tabs or collapsing the panel never discards a message.

Because a loop can run many times, each tab keeps only its most recent 1,000 messages. The summary line shows the total number of messages the run produced, so you can still see that older messages exist. While Messages is collapsed it does not reload the message list, but the run keeps collecting messages and updating the total, and the latest messages appear when you expand it again.

One message is limited to 4,096 characters so a very long Output value cannot fill the panel. A longer message is shortened, marked with …[truncated], and still ends with its own line break.

Messages belong to the run that produced them. A run that ends normally, fails, or is stopped keeps the messages it already produced. Starting a new run clears the previous run's messages. Clear Last Run, a new Template, and opening a Template all clear them with the rest of the Last Run. Messages are not saved to disk and cannot be exported.
